Brief: swesim as a hosted production pipeline on GCP, plus the overnight multi-model sweep

Written 2026-09-13 ~07:30 UTC (about midnight PDT) for the goal that runs until 2026-09-13 08:00 PDT (15:00 UTC). This brief is the detailed companion to the /goal text; the goal names the conditions, this document explains what they mean, how to verify each one, and what to do when something does not fit. Everything measured here refers to artifacts on disk or on the VM; nothing is asserted without a path.

0. Where we are (measured, as of this brief)

  • Code: main at 15bf683 (pushed). Offline suite 549 tests green; bash scripts/verify.sh 10 rc 0 against the laptop mirror of the VM record.
  • Orchestration today: one GCE VM swesim-worker (us-central1-a, project YOUR_PROJECT) runs the Temporal dev server (SQLite), one worker (single task queue swesim, max_concurrent_activities=16), and the console. Trials launch as transient user systemd units (swesim-trial-<id>), launch-once with reconcile; proven by the worker-restart and laptop-off evidence in workspace/evidence/ops.json.
  • Sandboxes: every image build, control run and graded trial runs through Harbor 0.23's Modal backend (harbor run -e modal). The verifier is a separate Modal container with no network. The stakeholder is a Modal web endpoint. Local Docker is optional smoke only. Daytona is not used.
  • Record: the workspace is a directory on the VM disk; scripts/vm/pull.sh mirrors it to the laptop. registry.json is tracked. 44 trial records; three valid scenarios (mwaskom--seaborn-3190 v2, scikit-learn--scikit-learn-13584 v2, py-pdf--pypdf-3826 v1, with a v2 rebuild running as create-22cefb3a…).
  • Stakeholder v2 measured: 12 Temporal trials on the two v2 scenarios, all reward 1.0; Sonnet 5 asked with intent and confirmed behavior in 4 of 4 interactive trials, Haiku 4.5 in 2 of 4; all 12 replies regenerated: false, no redactions. These two scenarios do not separate hidden from interactive for those models (see §5, difficulty).
  • Models in use now: judge openai/gpt-5.5, draft anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, stakeholder openai/gpt-5.5, solvers Haiku 4.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 (Anthropic) via Harbor's mini-swe-agent adapter. No OpenRouter path exists in the solver run (swesim/stages/run.py:PROVIDER_HOSTS knows anthropic and openai only).
  • Verified model ids on the configured keys (2026-09-13 07:20 UTC): OpenAI: gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini. Anthropic: claude-fable-5-1, claude-fable-5, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. OpenRouter catalog (prices per M tokens in/out): deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324 0.25/1.00, deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 0.27/0.40, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash 0.05/0.10, deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813 0.58/1.73, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash 0.15/0.60, z-ai/glm-4.5 0.60/2.20, z-ai/glm-4.6 0.43/1.75, z-ai/glm-5 0.60/1.92, z-ai/glm-5.2 0.60/2.00, z-ai/glm-5.3 1.09/3.43, z-ai/glm-5.3-flash 0.15/0.50, qwen/qwen3-coder 0.30/1.00, qwen/qwen3-coder-next 0.12/0.80, qwen/qwen3.6-plus 0.33/1.95, moonshotai/kimi-k2 0.57/2.30, moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code 0.71/3.50, minimax/minimax-m2 0.26/1.02, minimax/minimax-m3 0.30/1.20, openai/gpt-oss-120b 0.04/0.17, openai/gpt-5.6-luna 0.20/1.20.

1. Decisions taken with the user (2026-09-13, brainstorming)

Question Decision
Priority if not everything lands by 8 am Infra first. Temporal Cloud, GKE workers, IAP console, Cloud SQL live before the sweep; the sweep runs only on the new stack.
Temporal Temporal Cloud; the user is creating the account now and will place TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE, TEMPORAL_API_KEY in ~/Documents/.env. Client support exists (swesim.workflows.client.connect_kwargs).
Database Cloud SQL Postgres as the query index; GCS as the record of truth. Files stay authoritative; tables serve the console and the score tables.
Compute Cloud Run (GCP's ECS/Fargate equivalent; no Kubernetes): one Cloud Run worker pool per task queue, one Cloud Run Job per trial named by trial id, the console as a Cloud Run service behind IAP. Harbor inside the Job still executes on Modal. GKE was considered and rejected for tonight: it is the EKS equivalent and adds a cluster, RBAC, kustomize and External Secrets for no capability we need.
Creation scale SWE-bench pool A (all 109) + ten repositories (bugfix band): py-pdf/pypdf, pydantic/pydantic, fastapi/fastapi, encode/httpx, psf/black, pytest-dev/pytest, marshmallow-code/marshmallow, Textualize/rich, python-poetry/poetry, sqlfluff/sqlfluff.
Spend About $1,500 or more is acceptable, but the sweep must focus on cheap models (OpenRouter open models, OpenAI small models, Anthropic Haiku); frontier models only once the path is proven with trends. Spend tracked per run in the console.
Console access HTTPS load balancer + Identity-Aware Proxy, the user's Google account only, Google-managed certificate on a nip.io/sslip.io hostname unless a domain is named later.
Pipeline LLMs (judge, stakeholder, drafter) Very well-aligned frontier models only: judge and stakeholder on claude-opus-5 or gpt-5.6-sol (the user said "GPT 5.6 Soul"; gpt-5.6-sol is the id that exists — confirm the variant with the user; luna/terra also exist).
Evaluated agents Older-generation and newer-generation DeepSeek and GLM first, then other cheap open and small closed models; frontier (GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, Opus 5, gpt-5.5) only after the path is tested.
Tasks Must be hard enough: difficulty is measured, not asserted (§5).
Runtime (confirmed ~07:50 UTC) Cloud Run, not GKE. The user first asked about the ECS equivalent, then leaned GKE, then confirmed Cloud Run for tonight; the launcher contract and queue split are runtime-neutral so GKE remains a later Terraform module.
"GPT 5.6 Soul" Mapped to gpt-5.6-sol (the id that exists; luna and terra also exist). Opus 5 is primary for judge and stakeholder, gpt-5.6-sol the fallback, unless the user swaps them.
Primary objective (added ~08:20 UTC) Creating tasks from new repositories given as links is the main goal of swesim. Pool A (the 109) is the starting point and the calibration set, not the product. The sweep runs the repositories first, in both bands, with a per-repository discovery funnel in the console, and targets at least 10 valid repository-sourced scenarios by 08:00 PDT. No reward hacking (§7) and tasks and trajectories that are hard enough (§5) are explicit goals, not side effects.
Reusability (added ~08:35 UTC, refined ~08:45) Cloud-only. A stranger clones the repository, creates a GCP project and a Temporal Cloud namespace, puts their own keys in their env file, and follows docs/setup.md to a running hosted pipeline; docs/runbook.md covers operating it. No local or offline runtime is required (the offline test suite remains a developer check, not a way to run the pipeline). No path, hostname, account or file that exists only on the author's machine (Codex B10 is the checklist). Verified by a fresh clone into a new directory with a fresh env file.
Leaderboard (added ~08:50 UTC) By morning: a set of tasks (10–20 novel tasks from new repositories; the 109 too if time allows, or more), 3–4 models judged and scored, and a leaderboard page. Setting everything up correctly matters more than the size of the leaderboard, and a leaderboard on a bad task is worthless, so the no-reward-hacking work (§7) and the difficulty screen (§5) gate what appears on it.
UI/UX (added ~08:55 UTC) In parallel with everything else, the website must become a lot more aesthetically pleasing, with a better colour palette, better UX and UI, easier to use, and showing the right information. See §2.5.1.
Temporal Cloud (done 07:32 UTC) Namespace swesim.abcde in gcp-us-central1, API-key auth, 30-day retention, six swesim_* Keyword search attributes; service account swesim-worker (account role read, namespace write) owns a 90-day API key; values in ~/Documents/.env (TEMPORAL_ADDRESS=us-central1.gcp.api.temporal.io:7233, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=swesim.abcde, TEMPORAL_API_KEY); UI https://cloud.temporal.io/namespaces/swesim.abcde.
State at handoff (~09:00 UTC) Temporal Cloud namespace live (above). VM worker at 0333f4a connected to the Cloud namespace as an interim check only; the VM path is legacy and is not developed further. registry.json in the checkout is the legacy record and is replaced by the bucket root + Postgres; no pipeline output may be a git-tracked file after the redesign. Laptop main at d45fa7a; verify.sh 10 passes on the mirrored record (50 trial records, three v2 scenarios).
Console scope (added ~08:10 UTC) The website is the way we interact with the pipeline. It must show the entire database and every artifact in the bucket, and the complete history of everything that ever happened: every workflow, every trial including failed, unresolved and launch-failed ones, every candidate and gate reject, every scenario version. See §2.5.

2. Target architecture on GCP

All in project YOUR_PROJECT, region us-central1. Terraform under infra/ (no Kubernetes manifests; Cloud Run resources are Terraform). Nothing is applied by hand that Terraform can own; anything applied by hand is recorded in docs/ops.md with the command.

2.1 Orchestration: Temporal Cloud

  • Namespace <name>.<account> with API-key auth. Workers and clients read TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE, TEMPORAL_API_KEY (TLS on when the key is present; describe_connection logs only the auth mode).
  • Task queues (replace the single swesim queue):
    • swesim-authoring: mine, judge, draft, approve, scenario-version, archive, register, score, export. LLM-bound and light on CPU; high activity concurrency (32+).
    • swesim-build: probe, compile, validate (Harbor/Modal-bound). Concurrency capped (8–12) so Modal and the image registry are not flooded; heartbeats every 30 s.
    • swesim-trials: launch, await, reconcile of trial Jobs. Concurrency high (Jobs run elsewhere); heartbeating polls.
    • swesim-control: workflow-side bookkeeping (index writes, cost accounting, notifications).
  • Workflows are unchanged in shape (CreateTasksWorkflow → CandidateWorkflow children; RunTasksWorkflow → TrialWorkflow children). Each execute_activity names its queue. Existing REJECT_DUPLICATE / ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY semantics stay.
  • Worker versioning: every activity result and every trial record carries worker_image_digest (from the pod's downward API / an env var set by the Deployment). A result names the code that produced it.

2.2 Compute: Cloud Run (worker pools, Jobs, one service)

  • Why Cloud Run and not GKE. Cloud Run is GCP's serverless container runtime (the ECS/Fargate analogue); GKE is the EKS analogue. Everything this pipeline needs from a runtime is: long-running pull-based workers, an isolated container per trial with an idempotent "create once" primitive, an HTTPS service with Google login, mounted object storage, and native secrets. Cloud Run has all five without a cluster: worker pools for pull-based workers (no HTTP contract, instance-count scaling), Jobs for per-trial containers, services with IAP, Cloud Storage volume mounts (GCS FUSE), and Secret Manager references. GKE would buy per-queue autoscaling on Temporal backlog, which we would have to build anyway (custom metrics) and do not need tonight.
  • Workers: one Cloud Run worker pool per task queue: swesim-authoring, swesim-build, swesim-trials, swesim-control. Same image, SWESIM_TASK_QUEUE and MAX_CONCURRENT_ACTIVITIES per pool, instance counts fixed per pool (authoring 2, build 2, trials 1–2, control 1), CPU always allocated, the swesim-worker service account. Scaling is a Terraform variable per pool; a later step can drive it from Temporal's task-queue backlog. If worker pools are not enabled in the project, the fallback is a Cloud Run service per queue with min=max instances, CPU always on, and a 1-line /healthz server in the worker (documented in docs/ops.md).
  • Trial launcher = Cloud Run Job (SWESIM_TRIAL_LAUNCHER=cloudrun), implementing the existing contract (launch_once / read_evidence / decide_launch):
    • One Job resource per trial, name swesim-trial-<id> (Job names are unique per region: creating an existing name returns 409 AlreadyExists, which is the launch-once guard), task_count: 1, parallelism: 1, max_retries: 0, timeout ≥ solver timeout + 2 h, labels swesim-trial-id, swesim-scenario-id, swesim-run-workflow-id. After the Job is created it is executed once (executions.create); launch.json is written before the create call, so a lost acknowledgement is reconciled, never relaunched.
    • read_evidence reads the Job's executions (running/succeeded/failed counts, start and completion times) and the record files; decide_launch maps to launch / reconcile / completed exactly as the systemd version does.
    • The Job container runs the worker image with the same per-trial runner the systemd unit invokes today, against Modal, with provider keys, Modal token and the worker secret as Secret Manager references; the workspace bucket mounted at /workspace; 1 vCPU / 2 GiB (Harbor is a client; the heavy work is on Modal).
    • Housekeeping: a swesim-control activity deletes a trial's Job resource after its record is written and its execution has finished (logs stay in Cloud Logging; the record and launch.json are the evidence). This keeps the live Job count near the concurrent-trial count and inside the per-region Jobs quota.
    • Proof: a worker pool restart (gcloud run worker-pools update … --no-traffic-style re-deploy or instance recycle) during a running trial produces exactly one Job and one execution for that trial and the workflow completes (the Cloud Run analogue of the VM restart evidence); saved under workspace/evidence/cloudrun/.
  • Cloud Logging: worker pool and Job logs; a log-based metric on TrialWorkflow reconcile events; alert on worker pool instance crash loops.

2.3 Storage: GCS record + Cloud SQL index

  • Bucket gs://swesim-<project>-workspace (versioned, uniform access). Mounted at /workspace in the worker pools, the Jobs and the console as a Cloud Run Cloud Storage volume (GCS FUSE under the hood). The code keeps writing files; SWESIM_WORKSPACE=/workspace.
    • Known FUSE constraints to design around: no hard links, os.replace within one directory works (atomic_json is fine), fcntl.flock is not reliable across instances — the registry lock moves to a Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock) held by the register activity. Directory listings of thousands of trial dirs are slow: the console reads the index, not the bucket.
    • Import: the VM record is copied once with gcloud storage rsync (scenarios, tasks, trials without task copies, exports, candidates, evidence, registry.json, job essentials). VM-era trial records are labelled origin: vm-systemd in the index.
  • Cloud SQL Postgres (db-custom-2-7680, private IP, reached through Cloud Run's Cloud SQL connection or the Python connector). Schema (v1):
    • scenarios(id, version, spec_hash, source, source_ref, validation_status, compiled_hash, image_digest, difficulty_tier, created_at, registry_json)
    • candidates(instance_id, source, stage, status, reasons, judged_at, workflow_id) — the creation funnel
    • trials(trial_id, scenario_id, spec_hash, condition, brief_profile, model, run_config_hash, attempt_index, purpose, status, outcome_code, reward, success, started_at, finished_at, worker_image_digest, workflow_id, cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, origin)
    • exchanges(trial_id, seq, role, exchange, ts, request_id, disclosed_fact_ids, regenerated, redacted_terms, text) — evaluator-only columns flagged
    • scores(scenario_id, spec_hash, condition, brief_profile, model, run_config_hash, n, success_count, pass_at_k, pass_pow_k, mean_reward, questions_asked, confirmations, computed_at)
    • workflows(workflow_id, type, status, params_summary, started_at, closed_at, cost_usd)
    • costs(trial_id or workflow_id, provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, usd, at)
    • Written by the swesim-control activities at the end of each stage/trial (idempotent upserts keyed by ids); a swesim index rebuild command rebuilds every table from the files (the files stay the record of truth, the index is disposable).
  • Snapshots: bucket versioning plus a daily Cloud SQL backup.

2.4 Secrets and identity

  • Secret Manager: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, SWESIM_WORKER_SECRET, GH_TOKEN (read-only), MODAL_TOKEN_ID, MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET, TEMPORAL_API_KEY, DB_PASSWORD.
  • Cloud Run mounts them as environment variables from Secret Manager references (--set-secrets); the worker pools, Jobs and console run as the swesim-worker service account with secretmanager.secretAccessor, storage.objectAdmin on the bucket, cloudsql.client, and run.developer scoped to creating/deleting trial Jobs.
  • Never in images, manifests, Temporal payloads, logs, or the console. The laptop-copied /etc/swesim/env path is retired.

2.5 Console: the operator surface for the whole record

The website is how the pipeline is operated and how its history is read. Nothing an operator needs should require gcloud, kubectl, Temporal's UI or the CLI. Concretely:

  • Deployment: the same FastAPI app as a Cloud Run service behind an external HTTPS load balancer (serverless NEG) with a Google-managed certificate on swesim.<ip>.nip.io (or the user's domain) and IAP enabled with an allowlist of Google accounts; ingress restricted to the load balancer. The evaluator gate reads the IAP identity header (X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email, verified through the IAP JWT) against an EVALUATORS allowlist; ?evaluator=1 is removed. Evaluator-only data (author-only facts, hidden test assets, oracle, redacted sentences, tool audit, judge and draft metadata) renders only for evaluator identities; the public timeline never carries redacted_terms or withheld_sentences (Codex B-P2-6).
  • Data sources: Postgres for every list, filter, funnel, score table and trend; the bucket for artifacts. A page never globs the bucket to list things; it reads the index and links to the artifact.
  • History, complete: a Workflows page listing every workflow ever started (create, run, candidate, trial children) with type, status including failed/cancelled/terminated with the failure message, params summary, start/close times, cost, and a link to the Temporal Cloud UI; a Trials page listing every trial record and every planned-but-unresolved or launch-failed attempt, filterable by scenario, version, model, condition, brief profile, status, outcome, origin (vm-systemd / cloudrun), date; a Candidates page with the creation funnel (mined → judged → probed → drafted → approved → compiled → validated → registered) and every reject with its gate and reason; a Scenarios page with every version and its archive, the control table, the difficulty label and the build hashes.
  • Database browser: every table in §2.3 is browsable with filters, sorting, paging and CSV export; the schema page shows the index rebuild time and the last rebuild's diff against the files.
  • Artifact browser: a tree over the bucket (scenarios, tasks, trials, exports, evidence, candidates, archive) with file sizes, sha256 where the manifest has one, text preview for JSON/diff/log/toml files and download; evaluator-only paths are gated; the per-trial task copy (session token) is never listed.
  • Actions, all from the UI: create tasks (sources, band, models, approval mode, rebuild), run tasks (scenario selection with difficulty/tier filters, models, conditions, k, purpose, cap), approve/reject held drafts, cancel workflows, retry a failed candidate, label episodes (simulator validity), trigger an index rebuild; every action needs a confirmation step and a scheme+host+port Origin check (Codex B-P2-7), and is written to an operator_actions audit table with the IAP identity.
  • Live views: trials by state and queue, worker pool health, spend by provider/model/run (live ledger), the creation funnel as it moves, episode pages with the agent/stakeholder conversation streaming as it happens.
  • Measurement views: per-model accuracy tables by condition × brief profile (pass@k, pass^k, n; null when n is insufficient), trend charts (pass rate by model and condition as scenarios accrue; asked vs did not ask; questions and confirmations per trial; cost per solved task; difficulty distribution), model tier and difficulty labels everywhere a model or scenario is named. Charts follow the dataviz skill (one hue per model family, sequential for magnitudes, legend
    • table view, no dual axes).
  • Quality bar: consistent layout, keyboard-navigable tables, dark and light, no page over ~1 s on the index, every number linked to the artifact it came from.

2.5.1 Design: look, palette, UX

The console is the product surface people will see; it must read as one designed system, not a set of debug pages. Requirements, each checked before the cutover:

  • Design system. One typographic scale (a humanist sans for UI, a monospace for ids, hashes, diffs and logs), an 8-px spacing grid, a small set of surfaces (page, card, inset, overlay) in light and dark, consistent radii and borders, a single icon set. Tokens live in one CSS file; no page-specific colour literals.
  • Palette. Neutral surfaces with one accent hue for interactive elements; a categorical palette for model families (one hue per family, fixed order, never cycled) validated with the dataviz skill's validate_palette.js in both modes; a sequential single-hue ramp for magnitudes (pass rate, cost); reserved status colours for valid/invalid/running/failed/unresolved with an icon and a label, never colour alone. Status chips, table cells and charts use the same tokens.
  • Information hierarchy. Every page answers one question first: Home = "what is running and what changed", Scenarios = "what tasks exist and how hard are they", Trials = "what happened to each attempt", Leaderboard = "how do models compare on informative tasks", Review = "what needs a decision", Workflows = "what did Temporal do". The first screen of each page carries the numbers and the state; details unfold below or on drill-down. Ids and hashes are shortened with copy-on-click and a full value on hover.
  • Tables. Sticky headers, sortable columns, column filters, paging, dense but readable rows, right-aligned numbers, fixed-width monospace for ids, empty states that say what to do next, CSV export.
  • Navigation and flow. A persistent left nav with counts (running trials, candidates awaiting review), a global search (scenario id, trial id, workflow id, model), breadcrumbs, and every operator action reachable in two clicks with a confirmation dialog that shows exactly what will run (the CLI equivalent is displayed, as today).
  • Episode page. The agent/stakeholder conversation as a readable two-party transcript with timestamps, patience and exchange type, the question and confirmation highlighted, the submitted patch and test results beside it, and the evaluator-only material behind an explicit toggle for evaluator identities.
  • Leaderboard page. Models as rows, conditions as column groups, pass@k with n and a confidence note, cost per solved task, questions asked; filters for difficulty label, brief profile, scenario source (repository vs SWE-bench), model tier; a per-scenario matrix view; nothing shown without n, and saturated scenarios excluded by default with a toggle.
  • Charts. Follow the dataviz skill: form chosen by the data's job, one axis, legends plus direct labels, table view for every chart, hover tooltips, dark-mode steps validated separately.
  • Accessibility and performance. Keyboard navigation, focus states, 4.5:1 text contrast, no information by colour alone, pages under one second on the index, live updates without full reloads.
  • Process. A frontend stream works from a short design spec (palette tokens, type scale, page list, component inventory) reviewed against these requirements before the pages are rebuilt; screenshots of every page in both modes are saved under workspace/evidence/console/ and linked from docs/ops.md.

2.6 Build and deploy

  • Dockerfile.worker (python 3.12, uv sync --frozen, Harbor + Modal clients, swesim installed). Cloud Build trigger on push to main builds us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/<project>/swesim/worker:<sha> and :latest; digest recorded in the build log and passed to terraform apply as the image variable.
  • Deploy: make deploy SHA=<sha> = terraform apply -var image=<digest> (the four worker pools, the console service and the trial Job template are Terraform resources pinned to one image digest), then scripts/cloud/verify_cloud.sh. A GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch job with Workload Identity Federation does the same from CI (no long-lived keys). PR gating is not required (single contributor) but the offline suite runs on every push.
  • Terraform modules: network (VPC, subnet, Private Service Access for Cloud SQL, Serverless VPC connector or Direct VPC egress), registry, storage (bucket, versioning, lifecycle), sql (instance, db, user, private IP), secrets (secret resources; values set out of band), iam (service account and roles), run (worker pools, console service, Job template defaults), ingress (static IP, serverless NEG, managed cert, IAP OAuth client + allowlist), logging (log-based metrics, alert policy on worker crash loops and reconcile > 1).

2.6.1 Deploy path through GitHub

  • Identity: a GitHub Actions Workload Identity Federation provider in the GCP project and a deployer service account swesim-deployer (roles: Cloud Build editor, Artifact Registry writer, Cloud Run admin, Secret Manager viewer for the names only, storage object viewer on the Terraform state bucket, service account user on swesim-worker). No long-lived keys in GitHub; the repository holds only the provider name and project id as variables.
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml: on every push and pull request: uv sync --extra dev --frozen, the offline suite, the contract suite, ruff --select E9,F, terraform fmt -check and terraform validate. Required to pass before deploy.
  • .github/workflows/deploy.yml: on workflow_dispatch (with a sha input) and on tags v*: authenticate with WIF, gcloud builds submit the worker image tagged with the commit sha, resolve its digest, terraform apply -var image=<digest> (state in a GCS backend bucket, locked), wait for the pools and the console to become ready, run scripts/cloud/verify_cloud.sh, and post the digest, the Terraform plan summary and the verify output as the job summary. A failed verify marks the deploy failed and the previous revisions stay serving (Cloud Run keeps them).
  • Open-executions check: the deploy job runs swesim workflows open-types (a small CLI that lists open executions per workflow type through the Temporal client) and refuses to roll worker pools when a workflow type whose code changed in the deployed range has open executions and the change is not behind workflow.patched; the operator can override with an input that is recorded.
  • Local equivalent: make deploy SHA=<sha> runs the same steps with the operator's gcloud identity, for the night; the GitHub path is the documented way afterwards.
  • Versioned releases: the image tag, the Terraform variable and the worker_image_digest in every record all refer to one digest; git tag v<date>-<n> marks each deploy that ran a sweep.

2.7 What is retired, what remains

  • The VM keeps running until the new stack passes the smoke workflows; then its worker is stopped (systemctl --user disable --now swesim-worker) and the VM is documented as the fallback path in docs/ops.md. The Temporal dev server on the VM is not migrated (Temporal Cloud is a fresh namespace; workflow history restarts).
  • Modal stays for sandboxes and the stakeholder service.

2.8 Temporal design: what exists and what the goal must change

Measured against swesim/workflows/*.py at 15bf683:

Already proper. Two operator workflows (CreateTasksWorkflow, RunTasksWorkflow) fan out to one child per unit of work (CandidateWorkflow per candidate with id create:<sid>[@v<n>], TrialWorkflow per trial with id = trial id) under explicit id-reuse policies; per-candidate activities (judge_one, probe_candidate, draft, precheck_draft, auto_approve/human_approve, verify_approval, compile, validate, register, scenario_version, archive) and per-trial activities (plan_trials, launch_trial, await_trial, score, export); every blocking stage runs in a thread with heartbeats; await_trial is a heartbeating read-only poll with maximum_attempts=3; stage outputs are idempotent (existing output is retained, write-then-rename); payloads carry paths and ids, not bodies; launch.json before the launch call makes a lost acknowledgement reconcilable.

Not yet proper — required in the goal:

  1. One task queue (swesim) carries LLM calls, Modal builds, launches and bookkeeping. Split into swesim-authoring, swesim-build, swesim-trials, swesim-control (§2.1); each execute_activity names its queue; one worker pool per queue with its own concurrency.
  2. Retry classification. act() uses maximum_attempts=1 for everything. Temporal's rule: retry network errors, timeouts, rate limits and transient unavailability; never retry invalid input or business rejections. Activities must raise ApplicationError(non_retryable=True) for gate rejections, schema failures and "candidate not kept", and let transient provider/Modal/GitHub errors retry with backoff (3–5 attempts, initial 10 s, max 2 min). Launch stays at one attempt (the launcher is idempotent by design, but a retry must go through decide_launch, never a blind relaunch).
  3. Coarse activities. mine_activity for a GitHub repository does discovery and up to three Modal probe builds in one activity; split into discover_activity (GitHub only) and per-candidate probe_candidate_activity (already exists). validate_activity runs all seven control Harbor runs in one activity (10–25 min); split into one activity per control (validate_control_activity) plus an evaluate_controls_activity, so a single infrastructure failure retries one control, and the console can show per-control progress. The legacy whole-file judge_activity is used only by the legacy PipelineWorkflow; mark it legacy or delete it.
  4. Versioning discipline. No workflow.patched(...) anywhere; workflow code changed while workflows could be running (rebuild mode, band parameter). Every change to a workflow's command sequence ships behind workflow.patched("<id>") until no pre-change executions remain; worker deploys check temporal workflow list for open executions of changed types first; the deploy step records the check in docs/ops.md.
  5. Search attributes. Register swesim_scenario_id, swesim_model, swesim_condition, swesim_status, swesim_version, swesim_purpose (keyword) on the namespace and set them on every workflow start and on status changes (upsert_search_attributes), so the console and the Temporal UI can filter without reading files.
  6. Continue-as-new. CreateTasksWorkflow over 109 + repository candidates and RunTasksWorkflow over hundreds of trials must continue-as-new every N children (N = 100) carrying the remaining plan, so histories stay far below the event limit.
  7. Cancellation. Activities that run threads (blocking()) heartbeat but do not observe cancellation; add activity.is_cancelled() checks between stages and let the launcher cancel a Job on workflow cancellation.
  8. Payload hygiene. visible_view and forbidden terms are sent to the stakeholder over HTTP, not through Temporal; keep it that way; assert every activity input/output is under 256 KB in tests.

The single-model screen described below is retired as a gate; its label remains an informational chip recording what the screen run measured. The leaderboard admits every scenario that is valid and passes the task-sense audit (coherent ∧ fair_tests), whatever its label. Difficulty is read on /trends as the capability gradient (swesim/dashboard/gradient.py): accuracy by solver tier A→E per condition, with per-scenario chips — suspicious when a Tier A/B model beats the best Tier D/E model, saturated when every model with n ≥ 2 is at 100%. The frontier admission gate (swesim/stages/frontier.py) still exists, but the operator can proceed past a refusal with a recorded reason (swesim run-tasks --frontier-override "<reason>"); its "15 informative scenarios" clause is no longer how frontier runs are decided. Cost if wrong: an easy task inflates every model's score until the gradient chips flag it. The original text is kept below as written.

The user's requirement: the trajectories we see and the tasks we create must be difficult enough, and the creation process must find the right kind of tasks. Difficulty is a property we measure on every scenario and report per model tier; it is never asserted from diff size (CLAUDE.md) and never manufactured by editing a task after a gate.

"Hard enough" has a definition here: a scenario is informative for a model tier when the hidden arm does not saturate and the full arm is at least as good as hidden.

  • Screen: after validation, run hidden k=2 and full k=1 with openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 (Tier A/B boundary, cheap). Label: saturated if hidden 2/2 and full 1/1; informative if hidden ≤ 1/2; broken if full 0/1 (the brief plus facts still fails: suspect the task, look at the report). Labels live in scenarios.difficulty_tier and on the scenario page. Frontier runs skip saturated scenarios by default.
  • Sources of difficulty we can pull: the feature band (200–1,500 diff lines, ≥ 8 comments), contracts with more than one FAIL_TO_PASS test, withheld briefs with several removed spans, on-request facts the tests depend on. The creation funnel reports how many valid scenarios came from each band.
  • Reporting: the distribution of hidden pass rates per scenario for the screen model; the share of saturated scenarios; pass rate by tier. The existing v2 scenarios (seaborn, sklearn) are expected to be saturated for Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 and are kept as mechanism demonstrations, not as difficulty evidence.
  • Not done: hand-tuning tests to be harder. Difficulty comes from selection and measurement, never from editing a scenario after a gate.

6. Spend model and caps

Per-trial cost is estimated from measured token usage of the first trials per model and then tracked live:

  • Tier A/B open models: ~0.3–1.5 M input tokens per trial (context re-sent per step) → roughly $0.1–1.0 per trial.
  • Tier C: $0.3–2. Tier D: $2–8. Tier E: $5–25 (Opus 5 at $5/$25 per M; gpt-6-astra pricing unknown — measure one trial).
  • Validation: seven Harbor runs on Modal per scenario ≈ $0.5–2 in Modal compute, plus the drafter/judge tokens.
  • Planning numbers: 40 valid scenarios × (screen 3 + Tier A–C 18 models × 5 trials) ≈ 3,700 cheap trials is too many for the cap and the night; the goal therefore fixes Tier A–C at 6 models chosen across generations (older DeepSeek chat-v3-0324, newer DeepSeek v3.2 and v4-flash, older GLM 4.5, newer GLM 5.3, plus gpt-5-mini) for the full matrix, and runs the remaining Tier A–C models on a 10-scenario subset. Frontier: k=1 on the informative subset.
  • Hard cap: the console shows cumulative spend per provider; the goal's cap of about $1,500 is enforced by the operator (the user) and by a SWESIM_SPEND_CAP_USD check in RunTasksWorkflow that stops planning new trials when the recorded spend exceeds it.

Risk Handling

Harbor does not forward OPENROUTER_API_KEY Pass through the agent env option or [agent.env]; smoke trial before any sweep.
OpenRouter rate limits and provider routing variance Pin providers where OpenRouter allows (provider.order) and record the served provider from the response; cap concurrency at 20.
GitHub API rate limit during discovery of ten repos Sequential discovery per repo with the mine activity's existing pagination bound; spread over the authoring queue.
Cost overrun Spend ledger per run; SWESIM_SPEND_CAP_USD; frontier tiers gated.
Presentation at 16:00 PDT the same day Everything reported is measured; the fallback path (VM) stays documented and runnable.
